models.title: ArthroNat n
models.purpose: Insects and other arthropods: finds land arthropods on natural backgrounds (trained on the ArthroNat and flat-bug pictures).

models.title: MegaDetector V6
models.purpose: Common animals: finds animals in general (trained on camera-trap pictures, mostly mammals, birds and reptiles), plus people and vehicles.

models.title: flat-bug n (small)
models.purpose: Insects and other arthropods: finds any land arthropod on any background.

models.title: flat-bug s (larger)
models.purpose: Insects and other arthropods: finds any land arthropod on any background.
models.note: About four times the size of flat-bug n, so slower on the phone.

models.title: insectDCT detector
models.purpose: Insects on flowers: finds insects in camera-trap pictures of flowers and vegetation.

models.title: insectDCT classifier
models.purpose: Flower visitors: names insects in 104 fixed classes, from order down to species where it can.

models.title: insectDCT classifier (ConvNeXt-Base)
models.purpose: Flower visitors: names insects in 104 fixed classes, from order down to species where it can.
models.note: The authors' ConvNeXt-Base network. The EfficientNetV2-S one is offered for download.

models.title: insectDCT classifier (ResNet50)
models.purpose: Flower visitors: names insects in 104 fixed classes, from order down to species where it can.
models.note: The authors' ResNet50 network. The EfficientNetV2-S one is offered for download.

models.title: BioCLIP 2
models.purpose: Any organism: names what it sees, choosing from a name list.
models.note: Fast on phones whose graphics chip can run it.

name_lists.title: Flies, bees and wasps, beetles, butterflies and moths of Europe (35,264 names)
32 families of common flower visitors, worldwide (38,570 names)
Mammals and birds of the world (17,130 names)

models.title: BioCLIP 2.5
models.purpose: Any organism: newer and larger than BioCLIP 2, names what it sees from a name list.
models.note: Slow: on most phones it runs on the main processor only, seconds per picture.

name_lists.title: Flies, bees and wasps, beetles, butterflies and moths of Europe (34,704 names)
32 families of common flower visitors, worldwide (37,461 names)

uses.title: Pollinators on flowers
uses.setup: Fix the phone on a tripod, 15 to 20 cm above a flower or a group of flowers, so insects can fly in and out. On the camera screen, move the yellow square over the flowers: FaunaPulse looks for animals only inside it. If the insects look very small on the screen, bring the phone closer.

uses.title: Insects on a flat surface
uses.setup: Fix the phone on a tripod above a flat surface where insects land or walk (for example a coloured platform), looking straight down. On the camera screen, move the yellow square over the surface: FaunaPulse looks for animals only inside it.

uses.title: Mammals and birds
uses.setup: Fix the phone (on a tripod or a tree) facing a feeding site, a path or a nest entrance. On the camera screen, make the yellow square large, over the place the animals visit: FaunaPulse looks for animals only inside it.
